title: Abuse: Recognize It, Record It, Report It

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already treat injuries, protect yourself on scene and write PCRs. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Recognize child, elder and partner abuse, and sexual assault
  2. Write a PCR that works as legal evidence
  3. Know your reporting duty as the book describes it

Textbook: Chapter 46, PDF pages 3961–3993
slides.say: Welcome to class. Today's topic is hard but important: abuse. As EMRs, you already treat injuries, keep yourself safe, and write patient care reports. As a PCP, you're expected to see more: to notice when the story doesn't match the injury, and to build a record that could protect a victim in court years later. Today we'll cover three things: the patterns of child abuse, elder abuse, intimate-partner abuse, and sexual assault; how to document these calls so your report works as evidence; and what the textbook says about your duty to report.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来上课。今天的主题沉重但重要：虐待。作为 EMR，你们已经会处理伤情、保护自己、写病人护理报告。作为 PCP，要求你看到更多：发现病史和伤情对不上，并留下一份几年后可能在法庭上保护受害者的记录。今天讲三件事：儿童虐待、老年人虐待、亲密伴侣虐待和性侵犯的典型表现；怎样记录这类出车，让报告能作为证据；以及教科书关于报告义务是怎么说的。

slides.title: Why it matters
slides.body:
Child maltreatment, Canada 2008%
Neglect34
Exposure to partner violence34
Physical abuse20
Emotional maltreatment9
Sexual abuse3

About 85% of children who die from abuse or neglect are under 6; more than 40% are under 1.
slides.say: Why does this matter? Abuse is common, and you may be the only outsider who sees inside the home. In Canada's 2008 national data on child maltreatment, neglect and exposure to violence between partners were the largest groups, about a third each. Physical abuse was twenty percent, emotional maltreatment nine, and sexual abuse three. The youngest are most at risk of dying: about eighty-five percent of children who die from abuse or neglect are under six, and more than forty percent are under one.
slides.sayZh: 为什么这很重要？虐待很常见，而你可能是唯一能看到家里情况的外人。加拿大 2008 年的全国儿童虐待数据中，忽视和目睹伴侣间暴力是最大的两类，各约三分之一。身体虐待占百分之二十，情感虐待百分之九，性虐待百分之三。年龄越小死亡风险越高：死于虐待或忽视的儿童中，约百分之八十五不满六岁，超过百分之四十不满一岁。

slides.title: Safety first on abuse calls
slides.body:
• Agree on a code phrase with your partner to call police quietly
  • Keep your exit; stay calm and polite with everyone
  • Separate victim and suspect if you safely can
  • Hostile scene: clear bystanders; police if in doubt
  • There may be more than one victim
slides.say: Your own safety comes first, because an abuser who feels exposed may turn on you. Agree on a code phrase with your partner in advance: something ordinary, like asking for extra supplies from the truck, that really means go and call police. That way you don't tip off the abuser. Keep your exit clear and stay calm and polite with everyone, including the suspect. If you can safely separate the victim from the suspected abuser, do it; it's safer, and you can compare their stories. If the scene turns hostile, clear out bystanders and call police. And look around: there may be more than one victim.
slides.sayZh: 首先是你自己的安全，因为感到被揭穿的施虐者可能把矛头转向你。事先和搭档约定一句暗语：听起来很普通，比如让对方去车上拿点额外物资，实际意思是去叫警察。这样就不会惊动施虐者。保持出口畅通，对每个人都冷静有礼，包括嫌疑人。如果能安全地把受害者和疑似施虐者分开，就分开：这样更安全，还能比对双方的说法。如果现场变得充满敌意，就清走旁观者并叫警察。还要环顾四周：受害者可能不止一个。

slides.title: Child abuse: CHILD ABUSE clues
slides.body:
C consistent with development?A child's affect
H history doesn't fitB bruises of different ages
I inappropriate parent concernU unusual injury pattern
L lack of supervisionS suspicious circumstances
D delay in seeking careE environmental clues

Best indicator: the exam + a history that doesn't fit. Repeat calls to one home are a red flag.
slides.say: For children, the textbook offers the memory aid CHILD ABUSE. C: is the injury consistent with the child's developmental age? A baby who can't crawl yet can't reach the stairs alone. H: the history doesn't fit the injury. I: the parent's concern seems inappropriate. L: lack of supervision. D: delay in seeking care. A: the child's affect, or emotional state. B: bruises of different ages. U: unusual injury patterns. S: suspicious circumstances. E: environmental clues in the home. Repeat calls to the same home are a warning sign, but your best indicator is the physical exam combined with a history that doesn't fit.
slides.sayZh: 对儿童，教科书给了口诀 CHILD ABUSE。C：伤情与孩子的发育年龄相符吗？还不会爬的婴儿不可能自己爬到楼梯口。H：病史与伤情不符。I：家长的关注点不恰当。L：缺乏看护。D：延迟就医。A：孩子的情感表现。B：新旧程度不同的淤伤。U：不寻常的受伤形态。S：可疑的情形。E：家中的环境线索。同一家庭反复呼叫是警示信号，但最好的指标是体格检查加上与之对不上的病史。

slides.title: Child abuse: what the body shows
slides.body:
• Bruises at different stages of healing
  • Odd sites: buttocks, back, face, upper legs; bite marks
  • Stocking, glove or doughnut burns = held in hot water
  • Multiple fractures, or fractures at different stages
  • Head injury is the deadliest; belly injury rare but serious

Cupping and coin rubbing leave round red marks; a reasonable cultural explanation settles it.
slides.say: Soft-tissue injuries are the most common finding. Look for bruises at different stages of healing, and bruises where children rarely bump themselves: the buttocks, back, face, and upper legs. A burn with a sharp line around a foot or hand, like a sock or glove, or a ring-shaped burn with a spared centre where the skin touched the cooler tub, means the child was held in hot water. Multiple fractures, or fractures at different stages of healing, are red flags. Head injuries are the deadliest. But know the look-alikes: cupping and coin rubbing, traditional remedies in some Asian cultures, leave round red marks.
slides.sayZh: 软组织伤是最常见的发现。留意愈合阶段不同的淤伤，以及孩子很少碰伤的部位：臀部、背部、脸和大腿上部。手脚上边界整齐、像袜子或手套一样的烫伤，或者中间未烫伤、呈环状的烫伤（中间是贴着较凉浴缸底的皮肤），说明孩子被按进了热水里。多处骨折或愈合阶段不同的骨折是红旗。头部损伤最致命。但也要认识「相似物」：拔罐和刮币是部分亚洲文化的传统疗法，会留下圆形红斑。

slides.q: A father says his 2-year-old pulled a kettle of hot water onto himself. Both feet are burned up to a sharp line at the ankles, with no splash marks. What does this pattern suggest?
options: An accidental spill; the story fits
Immersion in hot water, an inflicted injury pattern
A cultural healing practice like cupping
A chemical burn from a cleaning product
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. A father says his two-year-old pulled a kettle of hot water onto himself. Both feet are burned up to a sharp line at the ankles, with no splash marks. What does this pattern suggest? A, an accidental spill; the story fits. B, immersion in hot water, an inflicted injury pattern. C, a cultural healing practice like cupping. D, a chemical burn from a cleaning product. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。一位父亲说他两岁的儿子把一壶热水拉翻浇到了自己身上。孩子双脚烫伤，烫伤到脚踝处有一条整齐的边界线，没有飞溅痕迹。这种形态提示什么？A 意外打翻，说法相符；B 被浸入热水，属于人为造成的伤型；C 拔罐之类的文化疗法；D 清洁剂造成的化学烧伤。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Stocking burns, with a sharp line around both feet, happen when a child is held in hot water, and in toddlers they're almost always inflicted. A spill from above would splash and run unevenly, so the story doesn't match the injury. Cupping leaves round red marks, not burns with a sharp line. Nothing points to a chemical. Treat the burn, document exactly what you see and hear, and report.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。双脚边界整齐的袜套状烫伤，发生在孩子被按进热水里时，在幼儿身上几乎都是人为造成的。从上面泼洒下来会有飞溅、流淌不均匀，所以说法与伤情不符。拔罐留下的是圆形红斑，不是边界整齐的烫伤。没有任何迹象指向化学物。处理烫伤，准确记录你看到和听到的，并报告。

slides.title: Behaviour clues and the exam
slides.body:
• Child: no reaction when the parent leaves; doesn't seek comfort
  • Child: cries constantly or not at all; wary of touch
  • Caregiver: vague about the injury, indifferent, or intoxicated
  • Caregiver: overreacts to the child's behaviour or condition
  • Toddler toe-to-head; infant in a parent's arms; respect teens
  • Examine with a colleague; record facts, not opinions
slides.say: Behaviour gives clues too. An abused child may not react when a parent leaves, may not look to the parent for comfort, may cry constantly or not at all, and may shy away from touch. Watch the caregivers: vague about how the injury happened, indifferent, overreacting to the child, or intoxicated. Adjust your exam to the child's age: start at the toes with toddlers, examine infants in a parent's arms, and respect older children's privacy. If you can, examine with a colleague. It confirms your findings and protects you against false accusations. And record only facts, not opinions.
slides.sayZh: 行为也有线索。受虐的孩子可能在家长离开时毫无反应，不向家长寻求安慰，可能哭个不停或完全不哭，还会躲避触碰。观察照护者：对受伤经过含糊其辞、漠不关心、对孩子反应过度，或者醉酒。按孩子的年龄调整查体：幼儿从脚往上查，婴儿在家长怀里查，尊重大孩子的隐私。如果可以，和同事一起查体，这既能核实你的发现，也能保护你免遭不实指控。只记录事实，不写个人意见。

slides.title: Elder abuse: subtle signs
slides.body:
• Active neglect: food, meds or help withheld; passive: ignored
  • Dirty, unkempt patient with a tidy caregiver
  • Capable patient, but the caregiver answers everything
  • Unexplained bruises, untreated sores, fear, isolation
  • Check: food in the fridge, temperature, walker, pill bottles
  • Care homes: undocumented pressure ulcers, tied-off catheters
slides.say: Elder abuse is growing as the population ages and caregivers burn out. It includes emotional and sexual abuse, neglect, and abandonment. Active neglect means deliberately withholding food, medicine, or help; passive neglect means the person is ignored or forgotten. Be suspicious of a dirty patient with a neat caregiver, or a capable patient who lets the caregiver answer everything. Look for unexplained bruises, untreated sores, fear, and isolation. Check the home: food in the fridge, the right temperature, a walker within reach. As a PCP, check the pill bottles: do the counts match the dates? In care homes, undocumented pressure ulcers and tied-off catheters are red flags.
slides.sayZh: 随着人口老龄化和照护者身心俱疲，老年人虐待越来越多。它包括情感虐待、性虐待、忽视和遗弃。主动忽视是故意不给食物、药物或帮助；被动忽视是老人被冷落、被遗忘。病人又脏又乱而照护者整洁，或者有能力回答的病人却让照护者代答所有问题，都要起疑。留意不明淤伤、未处理的疮、恐惧和孤立。查看家里：冰箱里有没有食物，室温是否合适，助行器是否够得着。作为 PCP，还要查药瓶：药量与日期对得上吗？在养老院，未记录的压疮和被扎死的导尿管是红旗。

slides.title: Intimate-partner abuse
slides.body:
• Four forms: physical, emotional, economic, sexual
  • Victims hide it: shame, money, fear of worse violence
  • Clues: changing story, no eye contact, self-blame
  • Men and same-sex partners are victims too
  • Ask directly about injuries; calm, kind, no judging
  • Refuses transport? Ask if it's safe to leave resource info
slides.say: Intimate-partner abuse can be physical, emotional, economic, which means blocking a partner from working or having money, or sexual. Victims often report it only as a last resort, because of shame, money, low self-esteem, or fear that telling will make it worse. Listen for clues: a changing story, no eye contact, or self-blame. Men and people in same-sex relationships are victims too, often with fewer resources. Ask directly about the injuries, stay calm and non-judgmental, and give the patient as much control as you can. If they refuse transport, first ask whether it's safe to leave information about shelters or victim support.
slides.sayZh: 亲密伴侣虐待可以是身体的、情感的、经济的（也就是阻止伴侣工作或拥有自己的钱），或性方面的。受害者往往到最后关头才报告，原因有羞耻、经济依赖、自卑，或害怕说出来会更糟。留意线索：说法前后变化、回避眼神、自我责怪。男性和同性关系中的人同样会受害，而且可用资源往往更少。直接询问伤情，保持冷静、不评判，尽量把掌控权交给病人。如果拒绝转运，先问留下庇护所或受害者援助的资料是否安全。

slides.title: Sexual assault: empower and preserve
slides.body:
• Any reaction is normal: crying, calm, numb, disbelief
  • Offer choices; let them do small tasks, like the SpO₂ clip
  • No need for details: ask how long ago and what since
  • Ask them not to wash, use the toilet, eat, drink or brush teeth
  • Bring clothing unwashed; keep a chain of custody
  • Young child: no genital exam unless bleeding or injury
slides.say: After a sexual assault, any reaction, from tears to numb silence, is normal. Your goal is empowerment, helping the patient regain control. Offer choices, and let them do simple things, like placing the oximeter clip. You don't need details of the assault; ask how long ago it happened and what they've done since. To protect evidence, ask them, if possible, not to bathe, use the toilet, eat, drink, or brush their teeth until the hospital can offer an evidence kit. Bring clothing unwashed, keep a chain of custody, and notify police per protocol. With a young child, don't examine the genitals unless there's bleeding or an injury to treat.
slides.sayZh: 性侵犯之后，从哭泣到麻木沉默，任何反应都是正常的。你的目标是赋权，帮助病人重新掌控自己。给出选择，让他们自己做简单的事，比如自己夹血氧探头。你不需要知道侵害的细节，只问发生在多久以前、之后做过什么。为保全证据，尽可能请病人在医院提供取证包之前不洗澡、不上厕所、不吃喝、不刷牙。衣物不洗原样带走，建立证据保管链，并按规程通知警察。对年幼的孩子，除非有出血或需要处理的伤，不检查生殖器。

slides.title: Document it like evidence
slides.body:
• Facts only: what you saw, found and heard
  • Patient's and others' words in "quotation marks"
  • No conclusions, like "beaten by husband"
  • Mistake? One line through it, then your initials
  • Names and contacts of witnesses
  • Court may come years later
slides.say: On abuse calls, your patient care report is evidence. Both the prosecution and the defence may use it, and you may testify years later, long after you've forgotten the call. So write only what you saw, found, and heard. Put what the patient and others said in quotation marks, word for word. Don't write conclusions like 'beaten by her husband'; write what she said and what you observed. Write neatly. To correct a mistake, draw one line through it and initial it. Record witnesses' names and contact details. A clear report also helps police and protective services decide what to do.
slides.sayZh: 在虐待案件中，你的病人护理报告就是证据。控方和辩方都可能使用它，而你可能在多年以后出庭作证，那时你早已忘了这次出车。所以只写你看到、发现和听到的。病人和其他人说的话放进引号，逐字记录。不要写「被丈夫殴打」这类结论；写她说了什么、你观察到什么。字迹要工整。改错时在错处划一道线并签上姓名缩写。记录证人的姓名和联系方式。清楚的报告也能帮助警察和保护机构决定下一步。

slides.title: Reporting: what the book says
slides.body:
• Child abuse: in most provinces, paramedics are mandated reporters
  • Use the toll-free line; don't assume the ED will call
  • Goal: protect the child, not punish the parent
  • Elder: record objectively for adult protective services
  • Care home: you may notify its regulator
  • When in doubt, report

Chapter 4: nearly every province requires reporting suspected child and elder abuse. Learn BC's exact rules.
slides.say: Now your duty to report, as the textbook states it. For child abuse and neglect, in most provinces and territories, the paramedic is a mandated reporter, which means you're legally required to report your suspicion. Never assume someone else or the emergency department has called; two reports of one case beat none. The goal is protecting the child, not putting a parent in jail. For elder abuse, record objectively so adult protective services can judge, and for a care home, you may notify its regulator. Chapter 4 adds that nearly every province requires reporting suspected child and elder abuse. Learn BC's exact rules, and when in doubt, report.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲报告义务，按教科书的说法。对于儿童虐待和忽视，在大多数省和地区，救护员是法定报告人，也就是说法律要求你报告自己的怀疑。永远不要假定别人或急诊已经报了；同一案件报两次也好过没人报。目的是保护孩子，而不是让家长坐牢。对于老年人虐待，客观记录，让成人保护服务机构判断；如果是养老院，你可以通知其监管机构。第四章还说，几乎每个省都要求报告可疑的儿童和老年人虐待。要弄清 BC 的具体规定；拿不准时，就报告。

slides.title: What the PCP actually does
slides.body:
• Tests the story against the injury with a full, careful exam
  • Treats injuries by the usual protocols, with every PCP tool
  • Uses the functional enquiry to uncover missed care or meds
  • Checks medications: missing, doubled, or not matching dates
  • Advocates for the patient; respects everyone, even the suspect
  • Shares findings with the ED and the right authorities
slides.say: So what does the PCP actually do differently? You assess more deeply: a full, careful exam and a history you test against the injuries. You treat injuries exactly as on any other call, with every PCP tool your protocols allow, like IV fluids for shock. Your functional enquiry, which only PCPs do, can uncover missed meals, missed medication, or untreated problems that point to neglect. Check medications for doses that are missing, doubled, or don't match the dates. Advocate for the patient and protect their dignity, while treating everyone, even the suspect, with respect. And pass it all to the hospital and the right authorities.
slides.sayZh: 那 PCP 实际上多做了什么？你评估得更深入：全面、仔细地查体，并用伤情去检验病史。处理伤情和其他出车完全一样，使用流程允许的所有 PCP 手段，比如为休克补液。只有 PCP 做的系统问诊，可以发现漏餐、漏药或未处理的问题，这些都指向忽视。检查药物有没有漏服、重复服用，或与日期对不上。为病人代言、维护其尊严，同时尊重每一个人，包括嫌疑人。最后把所有信息交给医院和相关机构。

slides.q: You suspect an infant has been abused. At the hospital, the ED physician says, 'We'll handle the report.' According to the book, what should you do?
options: Nothing more; the physician has taken over the duty
Make your own report as well, and document objectively
Confront the parents so they know a report is coming
Report only once police confirm the abuse
slides.say: Here's a decision for you. You suspect an infant has been abused. At the hospital, the ED physician says the department will handle the report. According to the book, what should you do? A, nothing more; the physician has taken over the duty. B, make your own report as well, and document objectively. C, confront the parents so they know a report is coming. D, report only once police confirm the abuse. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来做个决定。你怀疑一名婴儿受到虐待。到了医院，急诊医生说「报告我们来处理」。按教科书的说法，你该怎么做？A 不用再做什么，医生已经接手了这项义务；B 自己也报告一次，并客观记录；C 去质问家长，让他们知道要被举报了；D 等警察确认虐待之后再报告。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. The book says paramedics are mandated reporters in most provinces and territories, and you should never assume someone else has called; two reports are better than a case that falls through the cracks. A is wrong for that reason. C can put the child, and you, at risk, and it isn't your role. D is wrong because you report a suspicion; you don't wait for proof.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。教科书说在大多数省和地区救护员是法定报告人，而且永远不要假定别人已经报了；报两次也好过让案件漏掉。所以 A 错。C 可能让孩子和你自己陷入危险，也不是你的职责。D 错在你报告的是怀疑，不必等到证实。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Don't investigate or accuse: observe, treat, record, report
  • Look-alikes both ways: cupping; dementia "theft" may be real
  • Pill counts that don't match: overdose or withheld meds
  • Scald: BC cooling 15–20 min; fluids if burns > 20% BSA
  • Capable adult refuses? Respect it; leave info only if safe
  • After sexual assault: medication only if truly needed and ordered
slides.say: Finally, new watch-outs at PCP level. Your role is not to investigate or accuse; it's to observe, treat, record, and report. Watch for look-alikes both ways: cupping and coin rubbing are not abuse, and an older person with dementia who says money is missing may be confused or may be right, so document it either way. Pill counts that don't match can mean overdose or withheld medication. For scald burns, BC cools for fifteen to twenty minutes, and fluids start for burns over twenty percent of the body surface. A capable adult may refuse; respect it, but leave information only if it's safe.
slides.sayZh: 最后是 PCP 层面新的注意事项。你的角色不是调查或指控，而是观察、处理、记录、报告。双向留意「相似物」：拔罐和刮币不是虐待；患痴呆的老人说钱不见了，可能是糊涂，也可能是真的，无论哪种都要记录。药量对不上，可能意味着过量或被扣药。烫伤时，BC 要求冷却十五到二十分钟，烧伤面积超过体表面积百分之二十才开始补液。有决定能力的成人可以拒绝；尊重其决定，但只有在安全时才留下资料。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Story vs injury: CHILD ABUSE; elder neglect clues; partner abuse clues
  2. PCR = evidence: facts, exact quotes, one-line corrections, witnesses
  3. Report: mandated for child abuse in most provinces; when in doubt, report

Next: Chapter 47, Patients With Special Needs
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: compare the story with the injury. Use CHILD ABUSE for children, look for neglect and fear in older adults, and listen for hidden clues from partners. Two: your report is evidence: facts, exact quotes, one-line corrections, and witness details. Three: report as the book describes: in most provinces and territories, paramedics are mandated reporters of child abuse; never assume someone else called, and when in doubt, report. Through it all, keep yourself safe and protect the patient's dignity. Next time, Chapter 47, patients with special needs. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 记住三件事。一，拿病史和伤情对照：儿童用 CHILD ABUSE，老人留意忽视和恐惧，伴侣之间留意隐藏的线索。二，你的报告就是证据：只写事实、准确引用原话、划一道线改错、记下证人信息。三，按教科书说的报告：在大多数省和地区，救护员是儿童虐待的法定报告人；永远别假定别人已经报了，拿不准就报告。整个过程中，保护好自己，维护病人的尊严。下节课讲第四十七章，有特殊需求的病人。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
